results.name: OLIGO Security raises $60m to counter AI-speed attacks
results.content:
The round takes OLIGO’s total funding to $140m and drew backing from Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners, alongside angel investors including Eyal Waldman, ...
OLIGO Security, the runtime security company, has raised $60m in fresh funding as it races to help organisations keep pace with attacks that are now being planned and executed by AI at machine speed. The round takes OLIGO’s total funding to $140m and drew backing from Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners, alongside angel investors including Eyal Waldman, the co-founder of Mellanox Technologies, which NVIDIA acquired for $6.9bn.
OLIGO Security co-founder and CEO Nadav Czerninski said, “AI has fundamentally changed the economics of exploitation. When attackers can find vulnerabilities and build exploits at machine speed, runtime becomes the only place you can definitively understand true risk and stop attacks without impacting production.
The company said the raise caps a strong year of growth, with revenue climbing 300% year-on-year and its valuation more than doubling since its Series B. Over the same period, OLIGO was named by AWS as its exclusive AI runtime security partner for AWS Security Hub Extended, and it joined Palantir’s FedStart Programme to speed up its route to FedRAMP High and DoD Impact Level 5 authorisation.
OLIGO plans to put the new capital towards product development and expanding its go-to-market operations internationally, as it works towards its goal of helping businesses block zero-day and n-day exploits before they cause damage.

results.name: Oligo Raises $60M for Runtime Exploit Blocking
results.content:
# Oligo Raises $60M as AI Shrinks the Time Between Bug and Exploit  
[QUASA Editorial Team](https://quasa.io/team#editorial-team)|5 min read  
[Axios’s August 4 deals roundup](https://www.axios.com/newsletters/axios-pro-rata-f1a989ea-b33c-4058-a94b-4cfce74faa1c) listed a $60 million raise by Israeli runtime-security company Oligo Security. The participating firms were Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners.  
In its [August 4 financing release](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260804840699/en/OLIGO-Security-Crosses-%24140M-in-Total-Funding-with-%2460M-Round-to-Stop-AI-Driven-Attacks?utm_campaign=oligo_funding&utm_medium=top_announcement_banner&utm_source=oligo_website), Oligo put total funding at $140 million and said the capital would support product development and global go-to-market expansion; it also claimed 300% year-over-year revenue growth and described a platform that observes production code execution, prioritizes potentially exploitable vulnerabilities and blocks exploit attempts at the application layer. The growth and product-performance statements are company claims, not independently benchmarked results.
## AI is compressing the patch gap  
The financing rests on a specific security argument: exploit development can now move faster than an enterprise’s normal remediation process. Even after a patch becomes available, organizations may need time for compatibility testing, change approval, staged deployment and rollback preparation.  
[Anthropic’s N-day exploit study](https://www.anthropic.com/research/n-days) found that its Mythos Preview model produced a first working exploit in under an hour and ultimately created eight exploits from recent Firefox patches in roughly 12 hours under controlled evaluation conditions. The work does not establish that every disclosed vulnerability will be exploited that quickly, and turning an exploit into a real campaign still requires target discovery, delivery and evasion.  
It does support the narrower premise behind Oligo’s pitch: AI can reduce the specialist time needed to convert knowledge of a bug or patch into working exploit components. When that interval contracts, a monthly scanner or standard maintenance window may identify risk without providing protection during the period before a permanent fix reaches every workload.
## Funding does not settle the product case  
The transaction is labeled additional funding rather than a conventional Series C. Publicly available details do not include the security type, investor allocations, governance terms or a post-money valuation. Oligo’s revenue-growth percentage also lacks the underlying revenue figures needed to assess the company’s current scale.  
The distinction between runtime protection and permanent remediation remains important. A blocked attempt can reduce immediate risk, but it does not remove the vulnerable dependency, protect an unmonitored environment or guarantee that a different execution path will be covered. Patching therefore remains the durable corrective action.  
The financing verifies substantial investor support for Oligo’s runtime-security thesis. What remains unresolved is how the platform performs across varied production environments and whether the company’s claimed growth translates into durable enterprise adoption; independent benchmarks, retention data and fuller transaction terms were not included in the disclosed materials.

results.name: Oligo Raises $60M to Extend Runtime Security to AI Agents
results.content:
Startup Oligo raised $60 million to expand runtime exploit blocking to agentic AI, tracing activity from prompts and tool calls to system calls as faster
Oligo, founded in 2022, employs 129 people and has raised $140 million, having previously completed a $50 million Series B funding round in January 2025 led by Greenfield Partners. The company has been led since its inception by Czerninski, who previously spent more than six years leading the Israeli Military's cyber research team (see: Oligo Security Raises $50M to Tackle App Detection, Response).
The funding - led by Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital and TLV Partners - will help Oligo identify exploitation as it occurs and block it before an attacker causes damage, said co-founder and CEO Nadav Czerninski.
Czerninski said Oligo intends to use the funding to broaden the coverage and deployment options for its exploit-blocking capabilities. One use case is persistent protection against unknown vulnerabilities in software libraries that repeatedly produce security flaws.
Oligo continues to see conventional cloud-native applications dominate production environments, but Czerninski said it's also seeing growing use of applications built around LLMs and agents capable of making tool calls.

While the Israeli tech sector seeks stability, the domestic cybersecurity industry continues to heat up with the announcement by Israeli cyber startup Oligo Security that it has completed a $60 million financing round. The total capital raised by the company since its establishment in 2022 stands at approximately $140 million. The latest round was led by venture capital funds and investors Ballistic Ventures, Greenfield Partners, Red Dot Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and TLV Partners, along with Yasmin Lukatz and Eyal Waldman.
According to the company's announcement, the latest capital raise comes after increasing its annual recurring revenue (ARR) by more than 300% year-over-year, doubling its valuation since its Series B round, and expanding its operations. The additional capital is intended to accelerate product innovation and expand penetration into international markets. Oligo provides runtime security for applications, cloud environments, and artificial intelligence systems, combining runtime monitoring with real-time protection.
Oligo created protection for production environments without forcing organizations to choose between security and business continuity." The funding announcement comes just one day after US credit card and digital payments company Visa announced the acquisition of Israeli company BioCatch for $2.4 billion in cash, joining the approximately $2.6 billion raised since the beginning of the year by Israeli startups in the field.
Oligo Security was founded by CEO Nadav Czerninski, CTO Gal Elbaz, and CPO Avshalom Hilu, who are childhood friends and veterans of IDF cyber units in Military Intelligence (Units 81 and 8200) and the C4I Corps (Matzgov). The company currently reports employing about 100 workers, 70 of whom are at its development center in Israel, with the remainder at its offices in New York and San Francisco.

results.name: Oligo Security Raises $60 Million, Valuation Doubles
results.content:
Israeli cybersecurity company [Oligo Security](https://www.linkedin.com/company/oligo-security/) has secured $60 million in a new funding round after reporting sharp revenue growth and a doubling of its valuation since its Series B financing.  
The round was backed by Ballistic Ventures, Greenfield Partners, Red Dot Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and TLV Partners. Investors Yasmin Lukatz and Eyal Waldman also participated. The latest investment takes Oligo’s total funding since its launch in 2022 to approximately $140 million.  
The company plans to use the capital to speed up product innovation and strengthen its presence in markets outside Israel. The fundraising follows a period in which Oligo said its annual recurring revenue increased by more than 300% year over year, alongside an expansion of its operations.
#### Research brings Oligo Security wider attention  
Alongside its commercial expansion, Oligo has gained visibility through cybersecurity research involving AI infrastructure and widely used web browsers.  
In May 2024, its researchers uncovered an attack affecting thousands of servers used to train and operate AI systems. The servers had reportedly been compromised through a vulnerability that existing security tools had failed to detect.  
About two months later, the company identified another security issue affecting major browsers, including Chrome, Safari and Firefox. The weakness could allow a malicious website to bypass security protections and reach services running on a user’s computer or home network.  
Those services would normally be accessible only from within the device or local network. Browser developers subsequently updated their security mechanisms and moved to block the attack method.  
The discoveries helped reinforce Oligo’s argument that many serious threats become visible only when software is observed during actual use.
#### Founded by three childhood friends  
Oligo was established in 2022 by three childhood friends: CEO [Nadav Czerninski,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nadav-czerninski) [CTO Gal Elbaz](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gal-elbaz/) and [CPO Avshalom Hilu.](https://www.linkedin.com/in/avshalom-hilu/)  
The founders previously served in Israeli military cyber and technology units, including Units 81 and 8200 in Military Intelligence and Matzgov in the C4I Corps.  
The company currently employs about 100 people. Around 70 work at its development centre in Israel, while the remaining employees are based at its offices in New York and San Francisco.  
With new funding in place, Oligo is preparing to expand its technology and international reach while continuing to build around runtime protection. Its next stage of growth will centre on converting its recent revenue momentum and research profile into a broader position in the global application security market.
